newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street stocks seen opening higher.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street stocks seen opening higher.

text.p: Wall Street stocks are expected to move higher at the start of trading Monday with investors waiting for economic data due later this week.
Analysts said recent strong momentum could help boost the markets. But attention will focus on April retail sales figures due Tuesday.

"Right now it looks like we are heading for a higher opening...and a fall back as people square their positions ahead of the retail sales," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments.
A consensus estimate by economists calls for a 0.3 percent drop in retail sales. Excluding automobiles, sales are expected to rise 0.1 percent.

The data, among a raft of economic numbers coming out this week, could indicate the strength of the economy and whether the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) will raise interest rates at its May 20 meeting.

Thom Brown, managing director of Rutherford Brown and Catherwood, said such inflation measures as the Producer Price Index, due Wednesday, and the Consumer Price Index, due Thursday, "will set the tone for how serious people want to be" ahead of the FOMC meeting.
Tokyo stocks closed sharply higher. The 225-share Nikkei average rose 340.73 points, or 1.72 percent, to 20,143.51.
In London the FTSE 100 was flat at 4630.9.
U.S. stocks were firmer across the board in London after a weekend of upbeat reports on prospects for U.S. shares.

Microsoft Corp rose 3/8 to 117-7/8 in London on a Wall Street Journal report that it was expected to announce agreements with two companies to let users of terminals hooked up to a server computer to run most PC programs.
The dollar fell in Tokyo to just under 119 yen, hit by comments by Japanese officials about Japanese interest rates.
The dollar also fell against the mark, to 1.6933/40, on comments from a Bundesbank Council member that a further rise in the dollar could cause price problems in the long run.
The U.S. Treasury 30-year bond was up 1/32 to yield 6.89 percent. The Standard & Poor's 500 futures index was up 1.30 to 830.95.
The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street column said the crunch in the paper industry has hit Champion International Corp.
